title: Slides and horns: favorite instrument
summary: Willard mentions Quentin Jackson's slide; Young has two horns with different slides and tries new horns on small jobs first.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: The reason I asked, it never occurred to me that someone would have more than one slide.
Oh, yeah, they have more than one slide.

But I know when I was in Berkeley in May Quentin Jackson flew out to do a recording date with Kenny Burrell and he was complaining the whole time he was there that in his rush for the plane he'd taken the wrong slide. He was very upset that he hadn't brought his favorite slide.
He brought one that he -- well, it was acceptable, but it wasn't his favorite.

Yeah, there are -- there are -- in fact, they build some cases to carry two slides, but I try to get two slides built the same way as possible if I had to, but I don't have two slides. I got two horns, and there's different slide on each horn. But I usually have my favorite horn. Now, just -- just gave me a horn, a new horn yesterday but I don't know it well enough to bother with it right now. I'd be afraid to just jump up and play it on the job until I really know it, but when I get back

I can experiment on it on a little dance job that I'm playing. You know, it wasn't -- if it doesn't work right, it won't hurt nothing, you know. But you certainly wouldn't go on a concert and bring a horn like that out for the first time.
